newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police on alert over Shi'ite Moslem group.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police on alert over Shi'ite Moslem group.

text.p: Police in northern Nigeria have been placed on alert over an ultimatum given by a Shi'ite Moslem group demanding the release of its arrested leader, local newspapers said on Tuesday.

Police Commissioner Yakubu Shaibu urged the public in Kaduna to disregard the ultimatum by the Shi'ite Moslem Brotherhood which warned there would be trouble if its leader, Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky, and others were not released by Wednesday.

"We are equal to the task in jihad or holy war. Tell them unless they want to commit suicide we have our men on the ground and they are ready," the independent Guardian quoted Shaibu as saying at a press conference.
"If they dare us they will pay dearly for it," Shaibu added.
The Islamic group said on Saturday 14 people had been killed in clashes with police following El-Zak-Zaky's arrest on Thursday.
Police deny there were deaths, but say tear gas was used to disperse protesters in several northern cities after Friday prayers.
Shaibu said the Shi'ites were arrested for security reasons and said details would later be made public.
Mainly Moslem northern Nigeria has been the scene of sporadic religious riots. Last month three people were killed in a clash between rival sects in Kano, the region's biggest city.
Moslems, predominantly Sunni, make up roughly half of Nigeria's 100 million people. The exact figure is a matter of dispute.
